title: When the Detention Wakes
premise: Orsen Underhill has spent seventeen years perfecting invisibility in Hollow Creek, a town whose prosperity rests on the Founders' Detention, an annual ceremony no one will explain. When best friend Wren Vance vanishes, leaving only a ring of keys stamped with dates going back a century, Orsen follows the keys into the town's buried history and discovers the Detention is real: every generation, the town 'detains' one of its own children beneath the reservoir to keep the water—and the wealth—rising. Wren volunteered, believing sacrifice would finally make her belong, and she has until the spring thaw. To save her, Orsen must expose the truth to a town that would rather drown a child than lose its fortune, rally the misfits who become their found family, and confront the corrupt founding families—including Orsen's own grandfather—before the gates seal at the equinox.
about_author: Gideon Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent three years covering a reservoir dispute before turning to fiction. They write stories about quiet kids in loud towns, and dedicate this book to everyone who survived being the only one.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Unseen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establishes Hollow Creek's rhythms: the Founders' Detention festival, Orsen's careful invisibility, and their unshakeable friendship with loud, restless Wren, who keeps asking dangerous questions about the town's money. Emotional beat: the ache of a friendship that's Wren's lifeline and Orsen's shield.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Neighbors, One Secret
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Wren shows Orsen her research: the town's founders' ledger with a page torn out, and a pattern of one child 'relocating' every twenty-five years. Orsen begs her to drop it. Emotional beat: first fracture—Orsen's fear of exposure versus Wren's hunger for truth.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Wren doesn't come to school. Her mother reports her missing; police find only a set of antique keys on Wren's pillow, each stamped with a year. Orsen recognizes the oldest year from the ledger. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Reservoir Holds
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with a flashback to Wren. Following the first key to a maintenance tunnel beneath the dam, Orsen finds scratched messages from children across a century, all signed with the same symbol Wren drew in her notebook. Emotional beat: horror replacing grief.

chapters.title: The Founders' Detention
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Researching town archives with the help of Marisol, the librarian's granddaughter, Orsen learns the ceremony's true purpose: the town 'detains' a volunteer child beneath the water to sustain the reservoir and the founding families' fortune. Emotional beat: the tradition that made the town is a machine that eats children.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen breaks into the Underhill family home and finds their grandfather, Aldous, is the current Keeper of the Detention. He catches them—not with anger, but with a chilling offer: walk away, and Wren's sacrifice will be honored; speak, and Orsen becomes a target. Emotional beat: betrayal by blood.

chapters.title: Misfits at the Dam
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen confides in Marisol and Theo, a foster kid who's noticed the town's patterns too. The four form a fragile alliance in the tunnel, mapping the keys' dates to sealed chambers. Emotional beat: the first warmth of found family.

chapters.title: The Volunteer's Logic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, journal entries. Flashback revealing why Wren volunteered: years of being the town's charity case, promised 'belonging forever' by Aldous. She believed the lie. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness—Wren wanted to matter.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The founding families tighten the town: curfews, the librarian fired, Theo's foster placement threatened. Someone ransacks Orsen's locker and leaves a key missing. Emotional beat: the cost of visibility.

chapters.title: The Second Chamber
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Using a recovered key, the group opens a chamber and finds evidence a child survived decades ago—Descendant Ruth Ellery, now an old woman living at the town's edge, presumed senile. Emotional beat: hope has a face.

chapters.title: Ruth's Testimony
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV with Ruth's voice. Ruth recounts her escape and the Detention's mechanics: the gates seal at the spring equinox, and the 'kept' child sustains the water only while they hold on. Wren has weeks. Emotional beat: urgency sharpened by witness.

chapters.title: A Town That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen tests the town, hinting at the truth to classmates; parents shut doors, teachers change subjects. Even kind people choose the town over the truth. Emotional beat: loneliness of knowing.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo secretly photographs the tunnel evidence and contacts a regional journalist—but the story is killed, and Theo's tip is traced. The families know exactly who is digging. Emotional beat: courage meeting a wall of complicity.

chapters.title: Offer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Aldous makes a second offer: replace Wren. Orsen, the invisible one, could take her place and no one would ever know—except Orsen would finally, permanently, be seen as a sacrifice. Emotional beat: temptation and terror intertwined.

chapters.title: What Wren Left Behind
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, present tense. Below the water, Wren finds the previous kept children's messages and refuses to fade; she leaves a coded message in the chamber that only Orsen would understand—a reference to their childhood game. Emotional beat: defiance as love.

chapters.title: The Signal
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Decoding Wren's message, the group learns the gates can be opened from the old foundry control room—but only during the Detention ceremony, when the whole town watches the reservoir. Emotional beat: the plan crystallizes; fear becomes purpose.

chapters.title: Rallying the Nine Hundred
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol distributes Ruth's testimony and the ledgers through the school; some students join, parents split, and the founding families respond with intimidation. Emotional beat: found family becomes a movement.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The night before the ceremony, Aldous discovers the plan and has Theo detained; Ruth is hospitalized under 'care.' Orsen stands alone with the keys and a choice: flee with Wren's memory or walk into the ceremony. Emotional beat: the darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Detention Wakes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the ceremony, before all nine hundred, Orsen takes the stage, uses the master key to open the gates, and the reservoir's truth literally surfaces—the water drops, the old chamber exposed. Emotional beat: invisibility shattered into courage.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen descends into the draining chamber and finds Wren alive but failing; carrying her out as the town watches, Orsen forces everyone to witness what their prosperity cost. Emotional beat: rescue as reckoning.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Aldous and the founding families face exposure; some flee, some confess, the town fractures but survives—poorer, and honest. Ruth is believed at last; Theo is freed. Emotional beat: justice that costs everything and is worth it.

chapters.title: Head Up, Locker Open
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue. Months later: Wren recovering, the four friends inseparable, the reservoir renamed for the kept children, and a plaque with every name. Orsen, no longer hiding, speaks at the memorial. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not sacrificed for.
